dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: cittādyantaḥkṛtir nāsti mamāntar bhāvayed iti | vikalpānām abhāvena vikalpair ujjhito bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one contemplate: 'Within me there is no inner apparatus consisting of mind and the rest.' Through the absence of thought-constructs, one becomes free of them.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: when one is fully convinced through contemplation that one is not the psychic apparatus of mind (manas), intellect (buddhi) and ego (ahaṃkāra) with which one is always identified, the mind stops forming thought-constructs and one's essential nature, beyond them, is revealed as pure consciousness.
dharana.technique_name: No Inner Apparatus of Mind Within Me
dharana.instruction: Reflect, 'there is no thinking apparatus within me', and rest as the awareness that remains.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 94: There is no mind (Y70 ~ B3)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 94 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the habitual sense of a thinking apparatus inside
the reflection 'there is no such apparatus in me'
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the inner space where we usually locate a 'thinking machine', found to be empty, leaving awareness.
geometry.svg_hint: a head outline whose inside, usually drawn with gears, is left empty and softly lit
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Drop the machinery
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the sense of being a thinking machine is set down, and plain awareness remains. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The reflection: 'within me there is no inner apparatus of mind, intellect and ego'
attention.secondary: Awareness that remains when that identification drops

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one contemplate: 'Within me there is no inner apparatus consisting of mind and the rest.' Through the absence of thought-constructs, one becomes free of them.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sit quietly and reflect: 'Within me there is no apparatus of mind, intellect and ego.' Let the habit of identifying with thinking loosen. Rest as the awareness that remains.

honesty.disclosure: Door 071 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 71 (verse 94) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 071 is dharana 71, verse 94. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the reflection brings confusion or unease, let it go and simply rest with the breath. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
